comparator.name: Sociology
comparator.sourceNotes: The degree combines 75 EC of compulsory courses, 60 EC of major choices including the required bachelor project, and 45 EC of profiling electives.
components: Introduction to Research Methods and Statistics
This major elective complements the first-year sociology courses.
Advanced Sociological Theory: Modelling Social Interaction
Social Networks in Theory and Empirical Research
Take at least one of Social Networks and Family Sociology. This example takes both.
Pass the introductory and applied research methods and statistics courses first.
Pass Applying Research Methods and Statistics or Data Analysis Practicum first.
Choose 45 EC of eligible electives, including at least 15 EC at intermediate level or above.
Pass the 75 EC of compulsory major courses before starting the required project in the final two teaching blocks.

routeSelection.basis: Sociology and Social Research is the first recommended pathway in Utrecht’s student guide. This example follows that emphasis using courses that fit the timetable and degree requirements.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Sociological theory explaining how society, institutions and individuals shape one another
Social inequality, unequal opportunities and cultural or economic differences between groups
Families, neighbourhoods, religion, friendship and other social relationships
Quantitative social research, statistics, measurement and modelling with social data
Government, public policy and evidence-based responses to social problems
Independent sociological research culminating in the bachelor project
adjacent: Analysing digital societies through social media, network analysis, digital data and media power
Contemporary social problems, inequality, justice, environmental crises and public-policy responses
questions: Illustrative classroom and placement questions about alcohol use, religion, crime and youth behaviour
Graduate and postgraduate trajectories in research, consultancy, migration, policy evaluation and criminology

alternatives.label: Sociology and Social Research
alternatives.labelReason: The title reflects the emphasis and methods of the selected courses.
alternatives.concept: Study how institutions, relationships and inequalities shape everyday life. Combine sociological theory with interviews, statistical analysis and historical research to investigate how societies change.
progression: Introductory sociology precedes modern and contemporary theory. Research Methods & Statistics precedes applied statistical work and Econometrics. Histories of Gender and Modern History build context for advanced historical research.

alternatives.label: Sociology of Digital Societies
alternatives.labelReason: The title reflects the emphasis and methods of the selected courses.
alternatives.concept: Study how digital media and algorithms shape relationships, identity and power. Combine sociology and media analysis with programming, databases, data analysis and AI ethics.
progression: Programming, data and mathematical foundations precede machine learning and deep learning. Sociological theory and media analysis support the study of digital institutions.
alternatives.distinctness: This plan differs from the broad sociology plan by 11 courses and from the other focused plan by 8 courses in each direction.

alternatives.label: Social Problems and Public Policy
alternatives.labelReason: The title reflects the emphasis and methods of the selected courses.
alternatives.concept: Study how inequality, law and political institutions shape public problems and responses. Use social research, public economics and policy analysis to explore issues such as youth radicalization and environmental justice.
progression: Comparative politics precedes Public Policy Analysis, and Law, Society & Justice precedes Comparative Constitutional Law. Research Methods & Statistics precedes Public Economics and Econometrics.
alternatives.distinctness: This plan differs from the broad sociology plan by 7 courses and from the other focused plan by 8 courses in each direction.

candidates.label: Social Problems and Public Policy
candidates.assessment: Public economics, comparative constitutional law, policy analysis and communication support a coherent response to public problems and inequality.

candidates.label: Sociology of Digital Societies
candidates.assessment: Media history, AI ethics and sociological theory connect digital methods to social relationships and power. The technical courses support analysis without constituting a specialist social-network methods sequence.

selection.assessment: The broad sociology and methods plan and the two distinct directions in digital society and policy use the three available comparison slots.

blocks: Both introduce sociological concepts and theories for understanding institutions and social relationships.
Utrecht uses formal models to study social interaction. UCR examines a range of theoretical approaches in sociology.
Utrecht studies how social inequalities are measured and explained. UCR examines inequality in several courses, including environmental justice.
Utrecht studies explanations for a range of social problems. UCR approaches public problems through sociology, policy and law.
Utrecht introduces behavioral science through several disciplines. UCR introduces brain and behavior and studies social psychology.
Utrecht studies family formation and household relationships using quantitative research. UCR studies relationships and development across the lifespan.
Both introduce research design, measurement and statistical reasoning for empirical study.
Both apply statistical methods to data from social or behavioral research.
Both develop qualitative research design, interviewing and analysis through applied projects.
Both study prejudice and relations between social groups. UCR covers these within a broader social psychology course.
Both use data analysis in practical work. Utrecht emphasizes testing social-science hypotheses, while UCR develops broader data handling and visualization.
Both examine organizations, working relationships and the social processes that shape them. UCR also studies leadership.
Utrecht uses a supervised research practicum. UCR develops research experience in several courses.
Digital societies, networks, media and algorithms
Utrecht teaches dedicated social-network theory and research. UCR studies digital publics, media and relationships across courses.
Policy, politics and evidence-based responses to public problems
Both examine how policies are made and how institutions shape public decisions.
Utrecht teaches policy evaluation as a dedicated research course. UCR studies public policy and econometric methods in separate courses.
Personal development, bachelor project and profile space
Utrecht requires a 15 EC empirical research project. The UCR comparison shows optional independent research separately.
Choose 45 EC of eligible electives, including at least 15 EC at intermediate level or above.

notes.text: Utrecht offers dedicated courses in family sociology, social-network analysis and policy evaluation, followed by an empirical bachelor project. The UCR options combine sociological theory and research methods with study in related disciplines.
Utrecht reserves 45 EC for profiling electives. The UCR columns show complete examples of how students can select courses across disciplines.

audience.programmeDescription: Study how institutions, relationships and inequalities shape everyday life. Utrecht teaches mainly in Dutch, with some courses in English.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The Utrecht example emphasizes sociology and social research. The UCR options emphasize broad social research, digital society, or public policy and social problems.
